title: A Search Tree From Its Pre-Order

concept.title: Each value must fit between two limits; build while the next value fits
body: For a **search tree** the pre-order list alone is enough, because the order of the values tells where each one belongs. The first value is the root. The values after it that are smaller than the root belong to the left subtree, the others to the right subtree. Instead of searching for the split point, build the tree with **limits**: a recursive function `make(low, high)` builds the subtree whose values must lie strictly between `low` and `high`, and takes values from the list for as long as the next value fits.

body.code:
index = 0

def make(low, high):
    global index
    if index == len(pre) or not (low < pre[index] < high):
        return None                              # the next value does not belong here
    v = pre[index]
    index += 1
    root = TreeNode(v)
    root.left = make(low, v)                     # smaller values, at most v
    root.right = make(v, high)                   # larger values
    return root

body: Each value is placed once and never examined again, so the time is O(n). It is the same limits idea as in the "is it a search tree?" check, now used for **building**.

statement: The pre-order list (root, left subtree, right subtree) of a binary search tree is given. Rebuild the tree and print it in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The second line has `n` different integers: the pre-order list of a binary search tree.
outputFormat: The tree in level order on one line.
constraints: -10^9 <= every value <= 10^9, and all values are different
The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The root is 8, the left subtree has 5 (with 1 and 7), the right subtree 10 (with the right child 12): 8 5 10 1 7 N 12.

hints: The first value is the root.
A function with a lower and an upper limit builds a subtree from the next values for as long as they fit between the limits.
The left subtree uses the limits (low, root), the right subtree (root, high).

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.

    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))

    head = 0
    i = 1

        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":

explanation: `make(low, high)` takes the next pre-order value as a node when it lies strictly between the limits, then builds the left subtree with the limits (low, value) and the right subtree with (value, high).

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def from_preorder(pre):
    index = [0]

    def make(low, high):
        if index[0] == len(pre) or not (low < pre[index[0]] < high):
            return None
        v = pre[index[0]]
        index[0] += 1
        root = TreeNode(v)
        root.left = make(low, v)
        root.right = make(v, high)
        return root

    return make(-10 ** 18, 10 ** 18)

pre = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_tree(from_preorder(pre))
